elements.element: Transition assistance obligation triggered on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (i) ... provide reasonable transition assistance"

elements.element: Assistance available for up to 6 months
Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry/termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination ... (ii) within thirty (30) calendar days, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format

elements.evidence: "(iii) thereafter delete all such data and Confidential Information from its systems"
"certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing"
"within thirty (30) calendar days, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data"

reasons: The inserted paragraph (d) supplies every preferred atomic element: assistance on expiry or termination, up to six months, at then-current rates, 30-day data return, machine-readable format, deletion after return, and written certification of deletion.

"commonly used, machine-readable format" is the functional equivalent of the playbook's "standard machine-readable format"; the deterministic flag on this point is a wording nuance to note in the rationale, not a material gap.

The 30-day return clock runs from "expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason", not from a request; the "at Sparkling's request" condition attaches only to limb (i) transition assistance and does not swallow the mandatory data-return or deletion/certification duties.

Drafting is a concise single-paragraph insertion into a document that previously had no vendor-side exit/data-return duty, so it is minimal; no untouched sentence is altered and all surviving-provision and perpetual-licence mechanics remain effective.
Inclusion of "Confidential Information" alongside data broadens the return/deletion scope in our favour and "reasonable" mildly qualifies assistance; neither is an offending extra nor adverse to us.
Because the clause meets the preferred position, the fallback (90 days / 30-day export) is also comfortably exceeded; no further redline is warranted.
